headline: Ty Jerome scores 29, Cam Spencer has 24 as Grizzlies hand Hornets their 5th straight loss, 117-111
text: CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- — Ty Jerome made seven 3-pointers and finished with 29 points, and the Memphis Grizzlies handed the Charlotte Hornets their fifth straight loss, 117-111 on Monday night. Cam Spencer added 24 points and Cedric Coward had 16 points and nine rebounds for the Grizzlies, who limited the Hornets to 40% shooting from the field. Rookie Christian Anderson led the Hornets with a career-high 25 points on 6-of-8 shooting from 3-point range. Naz Reid added 24 points, Coby White scored 21 and Brandon Miller had 20 for Charlotte. The Hornets trailed by double digits for most of the fourth quarter and attempted to make a late run, but two of White's jumpers rattled in and out. That's been a trend in recent weeks as Charlotte has struggled to make shots from the field. Memphis had won five in a row before falling 104-95 at Minnesota on Saturday night. Jerome, the Grizzlies' leading scorer, appeared eager to start a new winning streak, hitting big shot after big shot and waving three fingers after each of his deep jumpers. He finished 10 of 21 from the field and 7 of 12 beyond the arc. Spencer also played with swagger, trash-talking Charlotte's Moussa Diabate after drawing a foul on a 3 and making all three free throws. Memphis played without rookie Cameron Boozer , the third pick in the draft who's expected to miss at least a month with a sprained right ankle. The Grizzlies were 24 of 24 from the free-throw line, with Spencer going 11 of 11. The Hornets were hoping to change the tide as they began a four-game homestand after losing all four games on a trip that ended Friday at Atlanta. Instead, they lost for the 11th time in 12 games. Up next Cavaliers: Host the Los Angeles Clippers on Wednesday night in an NBA Cup game. Hornets: Host the Chicago Bulls on Wednesday night in an NBA Cup game. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Deni Avdija hits 5 3s and scores 31 points as Trail Blazers hand 76ers only their 4th loss, 128-111
text: PHILADELPHIA -- — Deni Avdija scored 31 points and hit five of Portland's 19 3-pointers to lead the Trail Blazers to a 128-111 win over the Philadelphia 76ers on Monday night. The Trail Blazers crushed the Sixers all game with the long ball and handed them just their fourth loss of the season. Donovan Clingan had 15 points and 18 rebounds for Portland. Damian Lillard and Jrue Holiday each scored 18 points. Holiday made four 3s. Avdija was 4 of 4 on 3s and had already scored 22 points with 6:03 left in the first half just one game after Milwaukee's Tyler Herro scored 50 against Philadelphia. Avdija, the 25-year-old from Israel, had pockets fans that were scattered throughout the lower bowl of the arena chant his name and sing over the final minutes. Avdija acknowledged fans after the game with an appreciative wave and blew kisses to them as he walked to the locker room. Scoot Henderson and Holiday hit consecutive 3s in the third that ran Portland's lead to 96-87 and Jayson Kent hit the team's 16th 3 to close the quarter with a 101-92 lead. The Trail Blazers finished 3-3 on the six-game road trip that included losses on consecutive nights to the Minnesota Timberwolves . LeBron James scored 23 points, his most yet in a game in his first season with the 76ers. He hit his first four 3s of the game while the rest of the Sixers were just 4 of 23. The Sixers shot just 9 of 33 on 3-point attempts. Jaylen Brown scored 20 points in his return from a two-game absence with a hamstring injury and Tyrese Maxey added 22. Joel Embiid (illness) did not play for the Sixers who saw a five-game win streak come to an end. Trail Blazers coach Micah Nori got the win with his son Dante, a Phillies minor league prospect, watching courtside with Phillies general manager Preston Mattingly. Up next Trail Blazers: Host New Orleans on Sunday. 76ers: Host Miami on Wednesday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Siakam scores 20 and comes up big late as Pacers snap 4-game skid with 125-120 win over Thunder
text: INDIANAPOLIS -- — Pascal Siakam scored 20 points, including a 3-pointer with 44.4 seconds to go, and Kelly Oubre Jr . added a season-high 20 points to help the Indiana Pacers snap a four-game losing streak with a 125-120 victory over the Oklahoma City Thunder on Monday night. The Pacers finished 15 of 37 on 3-pointers and looked much more like the team that made the 2025 NBA Finals by pushing the tempo, knocking down long-range shots and spreading the scoring. Six players scored in double figures, including Jalen Slawson with 16, Andrew Nembhard with 15 and Ivica Zubac who had 14 points and 15 rebounds. Obi Toppin finished with 17 points and six rebounds. Two-time league MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander kept short-handed Oklahoma City close with 38 points. Kenrich Williams made four 3s and finished with 20 points, and Isaiah Hartenstein finished with 18 points and nine rebounds. But it wasn't quite enough to prevent the Thunder from suffering a second straight loss. What was supposed to be the first matchup between Tyrese Haliburton and the Thunder since Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals never materialized. Haliburton missed his 14th straight game with a strained left hamstring and only four of Monday's starters also started that Game 7 — Gilgeous-Alexander and Hartenstein of the Thunder and Nembhard and Siakam for the Pacers. Indiana never trailed after going on a 9-0 run to take a 27-19 lead late in the first quarter. The Pacers still led 56-51 and extended the margin to 70-58 in the third quarter before a back-and-forth final quarter. The Thunder cut the deficit to one twice in the final 1:31, but Siakam answered each time with a jumper, the second a 3 to give Indiana a 123-119 with 44.4 seconds left, and Oubre's late block of a layup preserved the lead. Up next Thunder: Return home to face Minnesota on Wednesday. Pacers: Get a three-day break before hosting Philadelphia on Friday. ------ See AP’s full MLB coverage here and See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Herro scores 32 points, Turner adds 27 as Bucks beat Raptors 116-111 to snap 13-game losing streak
text: TORONTO -- — Tyler Herro scored 32 points, Myles Turner fouled out with a season-high 27 and the Milwaukee Bucks snapped a 13-game losing streak by beating the Toronto Raptors 116-111 on Monday night. Kyle Kuzma scored 18 points and rookie Brayden Burries added 14 as the Bucks won for the first time since a 110-102 home victory over Indiana on Oct. 26. The 13-game skid was the second-longest in franchise history. Turner matched a season-high with 11 rebounds and made a season-best five 3-pointers, missing just once from long range. Scottie Barnes scored 31 points and Jakob Poeltl fouled out with 15 points and 10 rebounds, but the Raptors lost for the seventh time in eight games. After scoring a career-high 50 points in Saturday’s loss at Philadelphia, Herro had only three points in the first half Monday. He made six of seven shots in the third quarter, scoring 15 points. Herro shot 10 for 16 and went 4 for 5 from long range. He was 8 for 8 at the free throw line and led Milwaukee with eight assists. Toronto, which snapped a six-game losing streak by winning at Detroit on Friday, has not won consecutive games since the opening two games of the season. The Raptors have been without Kawhi Leonard (left knee) since, and are 4-11 in that span. Ja’Kobe Walter scored 15 points, and Jamison Battle and Immanuel Quickley each had 13 as Toronto fell to 0-6 at home in November. Collin Murray-Boyles (concussion protocol) returned for Toronto after sitting out Friday but RJ Barrett (right hamstring) was absent for the third straight game. Murray-Boyles had six points and 10 rebounds off the bench. Milwaukee led 85-80 through three, just the third time this season the Bucks have taken a lead to the fourth. They’re 1-2 in those games. Up next Bucks: Host Brooklyn on Wednesday. Raptors: Host Brooklyn on Friday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Jaden McDaniels scores career-best 34 for Timberwolves in 142-116 rout of Nets
text: MINNEAPOLIS -- — Jaden McDaniels scored a career-best 34 points and the Minnesota Timberwolves routed the Brooklyn Nets 142-116 on Monday night. Ayo Dosunmu added 23 as six Timberwolves players reached double figures. Terrence Shannon Jr . had 17 points and five assists off the bench, and Jonathan Kuminga scored 15. McDaniels shot an efficient 12 of 16 from the floor and made all four of his 3-point attempts. He hit a jumper early in the third quarter to reach 30 points for the third time in his regular-season career. The 6-foot-9 forward also had 10 rebounds and six assists. Minnesota set a season high for points, and Brooklyn allowed its most this season. The Timberwolves have won two in a row and four of five. The loss was the fifth straight for the struggling Nets. Julius Randle faced his former team for the first time since the Timberolves traded him to Brooklyn. After two seasons with Minnesota, Randle was dealt in the offseason as part of a four-team swap that helped the Timberwolves land point guard LaMelo Ball from Charlotte. Ball had 17 points in this one. Randle led the Nets with 29 points in his return to Minnesota. He was honored by the Wolves with a pregame video tribute. Mikel Brown Jr . added 17 points for Brooklyn, all in the first half. Brooklyn shot a season-best 50% from 3-point range (18 of 36), but a hot shooting night wasn't enough for a Nets team near the bottom of the Eastern Conference standings. Up next Nets: Play at Milwaukee on Wednesday. Timberwolves: Play at Oklahoma City on Wednesday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Bulls beat Cavaliers 122-108 behind Jordan Hawkins' 19 points and 63 off the bench
text: CHICAGO -- — Jordan Hawkins scored a season-high 19 points, Buddy Hield had 17 and the Chicago Bulls got 63 points off the bench as they held on to beat the Cleveland Cavaliers 122-108 on Monday night. Matas Buzelis added 15 points — all in the first half — as Bulls coach Tiago Splitter spread out playing time after a 151-145 overtime loss to Denver on Sunday. Tre Jones finished with 16 points and nine assists as six Bulls players reached double figures. Chicago shot 45.8% from the field and hit 20 of 49 from 3-point range. Donovan Mitchell led the Cavs with 28 points and James Harden added 21 after the 37-year-old guard scored 51 in their previous game, a 128-119 win over Indiana on Friday. The Bulls put it away with a strong fourth quarter, including a 10-0 spurt capped by Josh Giddey 's finger-roll layup 4:23 in that made it 113-97. Jones hit a quirky 3 with 3:56 to go to make it 120-104. Giddey was limited to four points, 11 assists and two rebounds in 22 minutes after posting 23 points, 14 rebounds and a career-high 22 assists on Sunday. Chicago was clinging to a 93-89 lead entering the fourth quarter after building a 24-point cushion with a big second quarter, when it outscored Cleveland 45-20. The Bulls led 72-50 at halftime. The score was tied 32-all a minute into the second period when the Bulls got hot — buoyed by their bench — while the Cavs went cold. Chicago opened the lead to 24 using a series of runs, including a 12-2 spurt. Chicago shot 49% in the half and hit 11 of 25 from long distance, with Buzelis nailing four 3s. The Cavs responded immediately in the third quarter, starting with a 9-0 run. They outscored Chicago 39-21 in the period to trim it to 93-89 on Mitchell's driving layup with 2 seconds left. Up next Cavaliers: At the New York Knicks on Wednesday. Bulls: At Charlotte on Wednesday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Jalen Green scores 25 and Devin Booker adds 22 to help the Suns top the Pelicans 123-119 in OT
text: NEW ORLEANS -- — Jalen Green scored 25 points, Devin Booker added 22, and the Phoenix Suns defeated the New Orleans Pelicans , 123-119 in overtime on Monday night. Collin Gillespie scored five of his 18 points in overtime, and Miles Bridges had 13 points and 11 rebounds for Phoenix, which won its fourth straight game while handing New Orleans its fourth straight loss. Jordan Poole scored 28 points — all in the first three quarters — and Zion Williamson added 25 points for the Pelicans, who've dropped 10 of 11 since starting 4-4. Saddiq Bey added 21 points and Jeremiah Fears had 11 assists for New Orleans. But Fears, who'd scored 29 points in a loss at San Antonio on Saturday, missed 14 of 17 shots against Phoenix. Trey Murphy also struggled as he works his way back from knee soreness that had sidelined him for seven of New Orleans' previous eight games. He shot 4 of 14 from the floor, and 1 of 6 from 3-point range. The Suns pulled away for good with a 10-4 run during overtime that included Booker's jumper, Gillespie's layup as he was fouled and Bridges' 3. Phoenix also led 109-107 with 31 seconds left in regulation after Booker's step-back jumper. Fears' driving scoop tied it at 109 with 22.8 seconds left, and Herb Jones' steal of Booker's pass in the final seconds of the fourth quarter forced overtime. Poole, who scored 25 points two nights earlier in San Antonio, made his first nine shots against Phoenix, including six from 3-point range. He scored 17 in the first half, after which Phoenix led 56-54. Derik Queen scored 11 points for the Pelicans, but missed four of five free throws in the fourth quarter, when the Pelicans missed six of 12 from the line. Up next Suns: At Houston in NBA Cup West Group A play on Wednesday. Pelicans: At Los Angeles Clippers in NBA Cup West Group B play on Friday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Kevin Durant scores 32 to power Rockets past Clippers 116-104
text: HOUSTON -- — Kevin Durant scored 32 points and Alperen Sengun and Amen Thompson each had 20 to lead the Houston Rockets to a 116-104 win over the Los Angeles Clippers on Monday night. Houston led by six points with about three minutes remaining before Durant made consecutive 3-pointers to make it 109-97. Brandon Ingram made a basket for Los Angeles but an off-balance 3 by Durant seconds later put the Rockets up 112-99 with 1:30 remaining. Ingram made his debut with the Clippers after sitting out since May following surgery for a heel injury and to repair a partially torn Achilles tendon. The two-time All-Star joined the Clippers in September from Toronto as part of the trade for Kawhi Leonard . He missed the last two games of Toronto’s first-round playoff series against Cleveland because of the injury. He had 16 points and seven rebounds in 27 minutes. Darius Garland had 26 points and eight assists to lead the Clippers, who lost their fourth straight. Rui Hachimura added 19 points. The game was tied midway through the third quarter before the Rockets used a 9-0 run, capped by a 3 from Tari Eason , to make it 74-65. Houston led by 10 entering the fourth. Up next Clippers: Visit Memphis on Wednesday night. Rockets: Host Phoenix on Wednesday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Luka Doncic scores 28, Lakers avenge loss to Jazz last week with 109-94 victory in rematch
text: LOS ANGELES -- — Luka Doncic had 28 points and eight assists, Jake LaRavia added 15 points and 10 rebounds, and the Los Angeles Lakers avenged a surprising home loss to the Jazz five days earlier with a 109-94 victory over Utah on Monday night. Matisse Thybulle scored 14 points for the Lakers, who have won 11 of 12 overall despite that 109-97 loss to the Jazz last Wednesday, ending a nine-game winning streak. Los Angeles struggled again in the rematch before breaking open a close game with a 17-5 run to start the fourth quarter. Kyle Filipowski had 21 points and 12 rebounds for the Jazz, who have lost three straight since beating both Los Angeles teams in back-to-back games last week. Utah is 3-16 this season, with more wins in Southern California than in Salt Lake City. After an impressive 12-2 start to the season while Doncic scored at least 40 points in seven games, the Lakers have stumbled through four home games over the past seven days, laboring each night against unheralded Charlotte, Utah and Sacramento — yet LA still managed to go 3-1. Not coincidentally, second-leading scorer Austin Reaves has missed five straight games with a heel bruise. Ace Bailey scored 18 points and rookie Darryn Peterson had 13 for Utah. Keyonte George managed only 14 points after scoring 30 last week against the Lakers. Doncic scored 14 points in the first quarter, but picked up his fourth foul during his scoreless second quarter. Los Angeles led by 16 points in the first half, but Utah made a 15-3 run out of halftime to take a lead. Prospective new Lakers owners Josh Kushner and Bob Iger watched the game with team governor Jeanie Buss. Up next Jazz: Host Denver on Friday. Lakers: At San Antonio on Friday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Castle helps Spurs stay unbeaten on road with 123-107 win over Kings minus Wemby, Fox and Harper
text: SACRAMENTO, Calif. -- — Stephon Castle had 28 points, 11 assists and eight rebounds as the San Antonio Spurs beat the Sacramento Kings 123-107 on Monday night without Victor Wembanyama and other key starters. Wembanyama sat out with back tightness after posting 50 points and 19 rebounds Saturday in a 114-91 win over New Orleans. De’Aaron Fox (shin) and Dylan Harper (hip) were also ruled out against Sacramento, yet the Spurs shook off a sluggish start and improved to 8-0 on the road. Julian Champagnie made six 3-pointers and scored 22 for San Antonio. He added seven rebounds, three assists and a block. Luke Kornet had 18 points and 11 rebounds, and Devin Vassell finished with 16 points. Domantas Sabonis had 20 points, 12 rebounds and eight assists to lead the Kings before fouling out. He shot 8 for 9 from the field. Zach LaVine scored 18, and De’Andre Hunter added 15 points, eight assists and seven rebounds. Sacramento led by 12 in the first quarter and dominated the paint early behind 10 points and six rebounds from Sabonis. Champagnie vaulted the Spurs into the lead with a personal 14-4 run, hitting four 3s to cap his 17-point second quarter. San Antonio outscored Sacramento 41-23 in the period for a 60-51 halftime lead. The Spurs used a 21-5 run in the third quarter to balloon their lead to 22 points, led by nine straight from Castle. Sacramento cut it to 102-94 in the fourth before San Antonio closed it out. The Spurs went 23 for 25 at the free-throw line compared to 9 of 14 for the Kings. Sabonis fouled out on Castle's drive to the basket with 3:25 left. Sacramento gave up 20 offensive rebounds and 26 second-chance points. Up next Spurs: At Portland on Wednesday. Kings: At Golden State on Wednesday. ------ A previous version of this story corrected that Wembanyama had 19 rebounds on Saturday, not 18. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here
